gloss: sixteenth night moon, night after the full moon

definitions.gloss: sixteenth night moon, night after the full moon
definitions.explanation: The night of the sixteenth day of the lunar month, when the moon rises slightly later than the full moon of the fifteenth night.

examples.japanese: {十六夜|いざよい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{月|つき}→月：02230_tsuki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{昇|のぼ}った→昇る：12960_noboru⟧。
{十六夜|いざよい}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{満月|まんげつ}→満月：17598_mangetsu⟧⟦より→より：09476_yori⟧⟦{少|すこ}し→少し：00596_sukoshi⟧⟦{遅|おそ}く→遅い：00533_osoi⟧⟦{出|で}る→出る：00513_deru⟧。
examples.english: The sixteenth-night moon rises a little later than the full moon.

examples.japanese: ⟦{秋|あき}→秋：02276_aki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{十六夜|いざよい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{眺|なが}め→眺める：02132_nagameru⟧⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧⟦{酒|さけ}→酒：02211_sake⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{飲|の}んだ→飲む：00322_nomu⟧。
examples.english: I drank sake while gazing at the autumn sixteenth-night moon.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
The word {十六夜|いざよい} comes from the verb ⟦いざ→いざ：28114_iza⟧よう (to hesitate, to linger), because the moon seems to 'hesitate' before rising on this night, appearing later than the previous night's full moon.

POETIC SIGNIFICANCE:
In classical Japanese poetry and culture, specific nights of the lunar month have names. The ⟦{十五夜|じゅうごや}→十五夜：24745_juugoya⟧ (fifteenth night) is the full moon, and {十六夜|いざよい} follows it. This reflects the traditional Japanese appreciation for the phases of the moon.

MOON PHASE NAMES:
- ⟦{十五夜|じゅうごや}→十五夜：24745_juugoya⟧: full moon (15th night)
- {十六夜|いざよい}: 16th night
- {立待月|たちまちづき}: 17th night
- {居待月|いまちづき}: 18th night
